h: Tips for a Top Day in the Driving Seat
p: A day at Diggerland is a bit like a day at the seaside: the more prepared you are, the more fun you'll squeeze out of it. Start with clothes. Think practical over pretty, because between the dusty tracks, the odd puddle and enthusiastic little drivers, nobody leaves looking spotless. A change of clothes in the car and a bag for muddy shoes will save you a lot of grief on the way home.

Get there early if you can. The first part of the day is when the queues are shortest, so you can tackle the headline machines first and come back to favourites later. In the summer holidays and on bright weekends the place gets busy, which is no bad thing for atmosphere, but it does mean a bit more waiting around. Snacks and drinks in the bag help keep small tempers in check.

Height and age limits are there for safety, so it's worth measuring the kids before you set off and having an honest chat about which rides they'll actually be able to do. It saves tears at the gate. Grown-ups, meanwhile, should be ready to be dragged onto just about everything.

Langley Park itself is a former mining village in the Browney valley, and County Durham has a lovely mix of countryside and heritage within a short drive. Lanchester is a pretty spot for a pub lunch, and the old railway paths that criss-cross the county are perfect for a gentle walk or bike ride to burn off any leftover excitement. Pair a morning of digging with an afternoon of fresh air and you've got a proper North East day out sorted.
